bird062: 0 -> 0
{
  "instance_id": "bird062",
  "db": "card_games",
  "question": "I collect promotional printings and play Brawl. How many different creature cards that have a promotional printing can serve as a Brawl commander? I just want a single number back.",
  "evidence": "A promotional printing is a printing of a card made as a promotion, as opposed to a regular set printing. Brawl is a Magic: The Gathering format; the deck's commander is the card that leads it, and only certain cards are legal as a Brawl commander."
}

SQL diff

--- before.sql
+++ after.sql
@@ -1,10 +1,13 @@
-SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) AS card_count
-FROM main.cards AS c
-WHERE instr(',' || c.types || ',', ',Creature,') > 0
-  AND instr(c.leadershipSkills, '''brawl'': True') > 0
-  AND c.name IN (
-      SELECT p.name
-      FROM main.cards AS p
-      WHERE p.isPromo = 1
+SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cards.name) AS creature_count
+FROM cards
+JOIN legalities ON legalities.uuid = cards.uuid
+WHERE instr(',' || cards.types || ',', ',Creature,') > 0
+  AND instr(cards.leadershipSkills, '''brawl'': True') > 0
+  AND legalities.format = 'brawl'
+  AND legalities.status = 'Legal'
+  AND cards.name IN (
+      SELECT promo.name

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cards.name) AS creature_count
FROM cards
JOIN legalities ON legalities.uuid = cards.uuid
WHERE instr(',' || cards.types || ',', ',Creature,') > 0
  AND instr(cards.leadershipSkills, '''brawl'': True') > 0
  AND legalities.format = 'brawl'
  AND legalities.status = 'Legal'
  AND cards.name IN (
      SELECT promo.name
      FROM cards AS promo
      WHERE promo.isPromo = 1
  )
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH type_counts AS (
    SELECT c.types AS card_type, COUNT(*) AS card_count
    FROM main.cards AS c
    WHERE c.watermark = 'boros'
      AND c.uuid IN (
          SELECT f.uuid
          FROM main.foreign_data AS f
          WHERE f.language <> 'English'
      )
    GROUP BY c.types
)
SELECT card_type, card_count
FROM type_counts
WHERE card_count = (SELECT MAX(card_count) FROM type_counts)
ORDER BY card_type
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH type_counts AS (
    SELECT c.types AS card_type, COUNT(*) AS card_count
    FROM main.cards AS c
    WHERE c.watermark = 'boros'
      AND c.uuid IN (
          SELECT f.uuid
          FROM main.foreign_data AS f
          WHERE f.language <> 'English'
      )
    GROUP BY c.types
)
SELECT card_type, card_count
FROM type_counts
WHERE card_count = (SELECT MAX(card_count) FROM type_counts)
ORDER BY card_type
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH japanese_printings AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        c.uuid,
        f.name AS japanese_name,
        c.type AS english_type,
        c.watermark
    FROM main.cards AS c
    JOIN main.foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid
    WHERE f.language = 'Japanese'
)
SELECT
    p.japanese_name,
    p.english_type,
    COUNT(r.id) AS ruling_count
FROM japanese_printings AS p
LEFT JOIN main.rulings AS r ON r.uuid = p.uuid
GROUP BY p.japanese_name, p.english_type
HAVING MAX(p.watermark = 'boros') = 1
ORDER BY p.japanese_name, p.english_type
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH japanese_printings AS (
    SELECT f.name AS japanese_name,
           c.type AS english_type,
           c.uuid,
           MAX(c.watermark IS 'boros') AS has_boros_watermark
    FROM main.cards AS c
    JOIN main.foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid
    WHERE f.language = 'Japanese'
    GROUP BY f.name, c.type, c.uuid
)
SELECT p.japanese_name,
       p.english_type,
       COUNT(r.id) AS total_rulings
FROM japanese_printings AS p
LEFT JOIN main.rulings AS r ON r.uuid = p.uuid
GROUP BY p.japanese_name, p.english_type
HAVING MAX(p.has_boros_watermark) = 1
ORDER BY p.japanese_name, p.english_type
LIMIT 1000

  "question": "I'm profiling how seasoned our Organizer badge holders in Germany are. Among the users who earned the Organizer badge and are based in Germany, how many had already earned 5 badges before they got the Organizer badge? Just the count, please. Note: \"before\" means strictly earlier - badges earned at the same moment as the Organizer badge don't count toward the 5, and the Organizer badge itself doesn't count as one of the 5.",
  "evidence": "Organizer badge: the badge whose name is Organizer."
}

Final SQL / answer

WITH organizer_awards AS (
    SELECT b.UserId, MIN(b.Date) AS organizer_date
    FROM badges AS b
    JOIN users AS u ON u.Id = b.UserId
    WHERE b.Name = 'Organizer'
      AND u.Location LIKE '%Germany%'
    GROUP BY b.UserId
),
qualified_users AS (
    SELECT o.UserId
    FROM organizer_awards AS o
    JOIN badges AS b
      ON b.UserId = o.UserId
     AND b.Date < o.organizer_date
    GROUP BY o.UserId
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 5
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS user_count
FROM qualified_users
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH organizer_awards AS (
    SELECT o.UserId, MIN(o.Date) AS organizer_date
    FROM badges AS o
    JOIN users AS u ON u.Id = o.UserId
    WHERE o.Name = 'Organizer'
      AND (
          u.Location IN ('Germany', 'Munich', 'Minga')
          OR u.Location LIKE '%, Germany'
      )
    GROUP BY o.UserId
),
qualifying_users AS (
    SELECT o.UserId
    FROM organizer_awards AS o
    JOIN badges AS b
      ON b.UserId = o.UserId
     AND b.Date < o.organizer_date
    GROUP BY o.UserId
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 5
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS user_count
FROM qualifying_users
LIMIT 1

{
  "instance_id": "bird132",
  "db": "codebase_community",
  "question": "I'm putting together the yearly activity report with a Germany-focused breakdown of who did the editing, covering posts created in calendar year 2012. For the 2012 posts whose last editor is a user based in Germany, I need the total score; and for all other posts created in 2012, I need their total score as well. Also, how many Germany-based users were the last editor of at least one 2012 post, and what their combined reputation is, as shown on their profiles. A user based in Germany is one whose profile location is in Germany.",
  "evidence": "A post's last editor is the user who made its most recent edit."
}

SQL diff

--- before.sql
+++ after.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+WITH post_scores_by_editor AS (
+    SELECT p.LastEditorUserId, SUM(p.Score) AS total_score
+    FROM main.posts AS p
+    WHERE p.CreaionDate >= '2012-01-01'
+      AND p.CreaionDate < '2013-01-01'
+    GROUP BY p.LastEditorUserId
+)
+SELECT
+    SUM(CASE WHEN u.Id IS NOT NULL THEN s.total_score END) AS germany_edited_post_score,
+    SUM(CASE WHEN u.Id IS NULL THEN s.total_score END) AS other_post_score,
+    COUNT(u.Id) AS germany_last_editor_count,
+    SUM(u.Reputation) AS germany_last_editor_reputation
+FROM post_scores_by_editor AS s
+LEFT JOIN main.users AS u
+    ON u.Id = s.LastEditorUserId
+   AND (u.Location = 'Germany' OR u.Location LIKE '%, Germany')
+LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH post_scores_by_editor AS (
    SELECT p.LastEditorUserId, SUM(p.Score) AS total_score
    FROM main.posts AS p
    WHERE p.CreaionDate >= '2012-01-01'
      AND p.CreaionDate < '2013-01-01'
    GROUP BY p.LastEditorUserId
)
SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN u.Id IS NOT NULL THEN s.total_score END) AS germany_edited_post_score,
    SUM(CASE WHEN u.Id IS NULL THEN s.total_score END) AS other_post_score,
    COUNT(u.Id) AS germany_last_editor_count,
    SUM(u.Reputation) AS germany_last_editor_reputation
FROM post_scores_by_editor AS s
LEFT JOIN main.users AS u
    ON u.Id = s.LastEditorUserId
   AND (u.Location = 'Germany' OR u.Location LIKE '%, Germany')
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH matching_posts AS (
    SELECT p.Id, p.Title
    FROM posts AS p
    WHERE p.Title LIKE '%principal component scores%'
),
linked_posts AS (
    SELECT l.PostId AS post_id, l.RelatedPostId AS related_post_id
    FROM postLinks AS l
    JOIN matching_posts AS p ON p.Id = l.PostId
    UNION ALL
    SELECT l.RelatedPostId AS post_id, l.PostId AS related_post_id
    FROM postLinks AS l
    JOIN matching_posts AS p ON p.Id = l.RelatedPostId
),
related_counts AS (
    SELECT p.Id, p.Title, COUNT(DISTINCT l.related_post_id) AS related_post_count
    FROM matching_posts AS p
    LEFT JOIN linked_posts AS l
        ON l.post_id = p.Id AND l.related_post_id <> p.Id
    GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title
)
SELECT c.Title, c.related_post_count
FROM related_counts AS c
WHERE c.related_post_count = (SELECT MAX(related_post_count) FROM related_counts)
ORDER BY c.Title, c.Id
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH related_counts AS (
    SELECT p.Id,
           p.Title AS post_title,
           COUNT(DISTINCT l.RelatedPostId) AS related_post_count
    FROM posts AS p
    LEFT JOIN postLinks AS l
        ON l.PostId = p.Id
       AND l.RelatedPostId <> p.Id
    WHERE p.Title LIKE '%principal component scores%'
    GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title
)
SELECT post_title, related_post_count
FROM related_counts
WHERE related_post_count = (
    SELECT MAX(related_post_count)
    FROM related_counts
)
ORDER BY post_title, Id
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH customers_with_fuel AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ym.CustomerID
    FROM yearmonth AS ym
    WHERE ym.Date >= '201301'
      AND ym.Date < '201401'
      AND ym.Consumption IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    c.Segment,
    COUNT(f.CustomerID) AS CustomersConsumedFuel2013
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN customers_with_fuel AS f ON f.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.Segment
LIMIT -1

    p.player_api_id,
    p.player_name,
    AVG(a.heading_accuracy) AS mean_heading_accuracy

  AND a.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY mean_heading_accuracy DESC, p.player_api_id ASC

Final SQL / answer

SELECT
    p.player_name,
    AVG(pa.heading_accuracy) AS mean_heading_accuracy
FROM Player AS p
JOIN Player_Attributes AS pa ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
WHERE p.height > 180
  AND pa.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY mean_heading_accuracy DESC, p.player_api_id ASC
LIMIT 10

Final SQL / answer

SELECT COUNT(*) AS transaction_count
FROM trans AS t
WHERE (t.k_symbol IS NULL OR TRIM(t.k_symbol) = '')
  AND t.account_id IN (
    SELECT d.account_id
    FROM disp AS d
    JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = d.client_id
    WHERE d.type = 'OWNER'
      AND c.gender = 'M'
      AND c.birth_date >= '1974-01-01'
      AND c.birth_date < '1977-01-01'
  )
LIMIT 1

{

  "db": "financial",
  "question": "I'm preparing a partner-bank negotiation and want to focus on our big-city clients. Please tell me, for 1998 (1 January through 31 December 1998), where the money went from gold credit card clients' accounts held at branches in large districts. Specifically: for accounts whose owner has a gold credit card, and whose branch is located in a district with at least 250,000 inhabitants, look at their outgoing payments (debit transactions, type VYDAJ). I need a ranking of the recipient bank and counter-account pairs by the total amount paid. If two pairs tie for the largest total, list both. For each pair, give me: the recipient bank code, the recipient counter-account number, the number of outgoing payments, and the total amount paid.",
  "evidence": "Gold credit card means card type 'gold'; account owner means disposition type 'OWNER'; the counter-account is the partner account at another bank to which a payment is sent; the district is the one where the account's branch is located."
}

Final SQL / answer

SELECT t.bank AS recipient_bank_code,
       t.account AS recipient_counter_account,
       COUNT(*) AS outgoing_payment_count,
       SUM(t.amount) AS total_amount_paid
FROM main.trans AS t
JOIN main.account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
JOIN main.district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
WHERE t.type = 'VYDAJ'
  AND t.date >= '1998-01-01'
  AND t.date < '1999-01-01'
  AND CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) >= 250000
  AND t.bank IS NOT NULL
  AND t.account IS NOT NULL
  AND a.account_id IN (
      SELECT dp.account_id
      FROM main.disp AS dp
      JOIN main.card AS c ON c.disp_id = dp.disp_id
      WHERE dp.type = 'OWNER'
        AND c.type = 'gold'
  )
GROUP BY t.bank, t.account
ORDER BY total_amount_paid DESC, t.bank, t.account
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH recipient_totals AS (
    SELECT t.bank AS recipient_bank_code,
           t.account AS recipient_counter_account,
           COUNT(*) AS outgoing_payment_count,
           SUM(t.amount) AS total_paid
    FROM main.trans AS t
    JOIN main.account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    JOIN main.district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
    WHERE t.date >= '1998-01-01'
      AND t.date < '1999-01-01'
      AND t.type = 'VYDAJ'
      AND t.bank IS NOT NULL
      AND t.bank <> ''
      AND t.account IS NOT NULL
      AND CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) >= 250000
      AND a.account_id IN (
          SELECT p.account_id
          FROM main.disp AS p
          JOIN main.card AS c ON c.disp_id = p.disp_id
          WHERE p.type = 'OWNER'
            AND c.type = 'gold'
      )
    GROUP BY t.bank, t.account
)
SELECT recipient_bank_code,
       recipient_counter_account,
       outgoing_payment_count,
       total_paid
FROM recipient_totals
WHERE total_paid = (SELECT MAX(total_paid) FROM recipient_totals)
ORDER BY recipient_bank_code, recipient_counter_account
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH account_loans AS (
    SELECT loan.account_id,
           COUNT(*) AS loan_count,
           SUM(loan.amount) AS total_amount_borrowed
    FROM loan
    GROUP BY loan.account_id
),
cardholders AS (
    SELECT client.client_id,
           client.gender,
           client.birth_date,
           card.type AS card_type,
           CAST(strftime('%Y', card.issued) AS INTEGER)
               - CAST(strftime('%Y', client.birth_date) AS INTEGER) AS age_at_issue,
           COALESCE(account_loans.loan_count, 0) AS loan_count,
           COALESCE(account_loans.total_amount_borrowed, 0) AS total_amount_borrowed,
           district.A2 AS district_name,
           district.A11 AS district_average_salary
    FROM card
    JOIN disp ON disp.disp_id = card.disp_id
    JOIN client ON client.client_id = disp.client_id
    LEFT JOIN district ON district.district_id = client.district_id
    LEFT JOIN account_loans ON account_loans.account_id = disp.account_id
    WHERE card.issued >= '1994-01-01'
      AND card.issued < '1995-01-01'
)
SELECT cardholders.client_id,
       cardholders.gender,
       cardholders.birth_date,
       cardholders.card_type,
       cardholders.age_at_issue,
       cardholders.loan_count,
       cardholders.total_amount_borrowed,
       CASE
           WHEN cardholders.loan_count > 0 AND cardholders.age_at_issue < 30 THEN 'Young borrower'
           WHEN cardholders.loan_count > 0 AND cardholders.age_at_issue >= 30 THEN 'Mature borrower'
           ELSE 'Non-borrower'
       END AS borrower_classification,
       cardholders.district_name,
       cardholders.district_average_salary,
       RANK() OVER (
           PARTITION BY cardholders.gender
           ORDER BY cardholders.age_at_issue DESC
       ) AS age_rank_within_gender
FROM cardholders
ORDER BY cardholders.client_id
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH cardholders AS (
    SELECT
        cl.client_id,
        cl.gender,
        cl.birth_date,
        c.type AS card_type,
        CAST(strftime('%Y', c.issued) AS INTEGER)
            - CAST(strftime('%Y', cl.birth_date) AS INTEGER) AS age_at_card_issue,
        dp.account_id,
        cl.district_id
    FROM main.card AS c
    JOIN main.disp AS dp ON dp.disp_id = c.disp_id
    JOIN main.client AS cl ON cl.client_id = dp.client_id
    WHERE c.issued >= '1994-01-01' AND c.issued < '1995-01-01'
),
account_loans AS (
    SELECT
        l.account_id,
        COUNT(*) AS number_of_loans,
        SUM(l.amount) AS total_amount_borrowed
    FROM main.loan AS l
    GROUP BY l.account_id
)
SELECT
    ch.client_id,
    ch.gender,
    ch.birth_date,
    ch.card_type,
    ch.age_at_card_issue,
    COALESCE(al.number_of_loans, 0) AS number_of_loans,
    COALESCE(al.total_amount_borrowed, 0) AS total_amount_borrowed,
    CASE
        WHEN al.number_of_loans > 0 AND ch.age_at_card_issue < 30 THEN 'Young borrower'
        WHEN al.number_of_loans > 0 AND ch.age_at_card_issue >= 30 THEN 'Mature borrower'
        ELSE 'Non-borrower'
    END AS borrower_classification,
    dt.A2 AS district_name,
    dt.A11 AS district_average_salary,
    RANK() OVER (
        PARTITION BY ch.gender
        ORDER BY ch.age_at_card_issue DESC
    ) AS age_rank_within_gender
FROM cardholders AS ch
LEFT JOIN account_loans AS al ON al.account_id = ch.account_id
LEFT JOIN main.district AS dt ON dt.district_id = ch.district_id
ORDER BY ch.client_id
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH race_winner_times AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT r.year, r.raceId, res.milliseconds
    FROM main.races AS r
    JOIN main.results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId
    WHERE r.year < 1975
      AND res.position = 1
      AND res.milliseconds IS NOT NULL
),
yearly_totals AS (
    SELECT year, SUM(milliseconds) AS total_ms, COUNT(*) AS race_count
    FROM race_winner_times
    GROUP BY year
)
SELECT
    year,
    ((total_ms + 5 * race_count) / (10 * race_count)) / 100.0
        AS mean_winner_elapsed_seconds
FROM yearly_totals
ORDER BY year
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH race_winner_times AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT r.year, r.raceId, res.milliseconds
    FROM races AS r
    JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId
    WHERE r.year < 1975
      AND res.position = 1
      AND res.milliseconds IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    year,
    ((SUM(milliseconds) + 5 * COUNT(*)) / (10 * COUNT(*))) / 100.0
        AS mean_winner_elapsed_seconds
FROM race_winner_times
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 1000

SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d.forename = 'Peter' THEN d.driverId END) AS Peter,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d.forename = 'John' THEN d.driverId END) AS John
FROM main.drivers AS d
JOIN main.results AS r ON r.driverId = d.driverId
WHERE d.forename IN ('Peter', 'John')
  AND r.position = 1
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH members_per_major AS (
    SELECT link_to_major AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS member_count
    FROM main.member
    GROUP BY link_to_major
),
department_majors AS (
    SELECT
        catalog.department,
        catalog.major_name,
        catalog.college,
        COALESCE(roster.member_count, 0) AS member_count
    FROM main.major AS catalog
    LEFT JOIN members_per_major AS roster ON roster.major_id = catalog.major_id
    ORDER BY catalog.department, catalog.major_name, catalog.major_id
)
SELECT
    department AS department_name,
    GROUP_CONCAT(major_name, ', ') AS majors_offered,
    GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN member_count > 0 THEN major_name END, ', ') AS majors_held,
    ROUND(AVG(member_count), 2) AS average_members_per_major
FROM department_majors
GROUP BY department
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' THEN 1 END) > 0
ORDER BY department
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH member_counts AS (
    SELECT mb.link_to_major, COUNT(*) AS member_count
    FROM main.member AS mb
    GROUP BY mb.link_to_major
)
SELECT
    m.department,
    GROUP_CONCAT(m.major_name, ', ' ORDER BY m.major_name) AS majors_offered,
    GROUP_CONCAT(m.major_name, ', ' ORDER BY m.major_name)
        FILTER (WHERE mc.member_count > 0) AS majors_held_by_members,
    ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(mc.member_count, 0)), 2) AS avg_members_per_major
FROM main.major AS m
LEFT JOIN member_counts AS mc ON mc.link_to_major = m.major_id
GROUP BY m.department
HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences') > 0
ORDER BY m.department
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH latest_vice_president_expense AS (
    SELECT MAX(e.expense_date) AS expense_date
    FROM expense AS e
    JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member
    WHERE m.position = 'Vice President'
)
SELECT e.expense_date, SUM(e.cost) AS total_cost
FROM expense AS e
JOIN latest_vice_president_expense AS latest
    ON latest.expense_date = e.expense_date
GROUP BY e.expense_date
LIMIT 1

    SELECT MAX(e.expense_date) AS expense_date
    FROM main.expense AS e
    JOIN main.member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member
    WHERE m.position = 'Vice President'

FROM main.expense AS e

GROUP BY e.expense_date

Final SQL / answer

WITH budget_by_event AS (
    SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) AS total_budgeted
    FROM main.budget
    GROUP BY link_to_event
),
attendance_by_event AS (
    SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(link_to_member) AS members_attended
    FROM main.attendance
    GROUP BY link_to_event
)
SELECT e.event_name,
       e.event_date,
       b.total_budgeted,
       COALESCE(a.members_attended, 0) AS members_attended
FROM main.event AS e
LEFT JOIN budget_by_event AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
LEFT JOIN attendance_by_event AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id
ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC
LIMIT -1

Final SQL / answer

WITH event_budgets AS (
    SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(b.amount) AS total_budgeted
    FROM budget AS b
    GROUP BY b.link_to_event
),
event_attendance AS (
    SELECT a.link_to_event, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS members_attended
    FROM attendance AS a
    GROUP BY a.link_to_event
)
SELECT
    e.event_name,
    e.event_date,
    b.total_budgeted,
    COALESCE(a.members_attended, 0) AS members_attended
FROM event AS e
LEFT JOIN event_budgets AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
LEFT JOIN event_attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id
ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH RECURSIVE items(expense_id, item_name, remaining) AS (
    SELECT e.expense_id,
           '',
           CASE
               WHEN e.expense_description LIKE 'Bakery - %'
               THEN substr(e.expense_description, length('Bakery - ') + 1)
               ELSE e.expense_description
           END || ','
    FROM expense AS e
    JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member
    WHERE m.first_name = 'Sacha'
      AND m.last_name = 'Harrison'

    UNION ALL

    SELECT expense_id,
           trim(substr(remaining, 1, instr(remaining, ',') - 1)),
           substr(remaining, instr(remaining, ',') + 1)
    FROM items
    WHERE remaining <> ''
)
SELECT item_name, COUNT(DISTINCT expense_id) AS purchase_count
FROM items
WHERE item_name <> ''
GROUP BY item_name
ORDER BY item_name
LIMIT -1

WITH RECURSIVE descriptions(description) AS (
    SELECT CASE
               WHEN e.expense_description GLOB 'Bakery - *'
               THEN substr(e.expense_description, length('Bakery - ') + 1)
               ELSE e.expense_description
           END
    FROM main.expense AS e
    JOIN main.member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member
    WHERE m.first_name = 'Sacha'
      AND m.last_name = 'Harrison'
),
items(item_name, remaining) AS (
    SELECT '', description || ','
    FROM descriptions
    UNION ALL
    SELECT trim(substr(remaining, 1, instr(remaining, ',') - 1)),
           substr(remaining, instr(remaining, ',') + 1)
    FROM items
    WHERE remaining <> ''
)
SELECT item_name, COUNT(*) AS purchase_count
FROM items
WHERE item_name <> ''
GROUP BY item_name
ORDER BY item_name
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH RECURSIVE
period_expenses AS (
    SELECT e.link_to_member AS member_id, e.expense_description, e.cost
    FROM main.expense AS e
    WHERE e.expense_date >= '2019-10-01'
      AND e.expense_date < '2019-12-01'
),
item_parts(member_id, item, remainder) AS (
    SELECT member_id, NULL, expense_description || ','
    FROM period_expenses
    UNION ALL
    SELECT member_id,
           SUBSTR(remainder, 1, INSTR(remainder, ',') - 1),
           SUBSTR(remainder, INSTR(remainder, ',') + 1)
    FROM item_parts
    WHERE remainder <> ''
),
item_counts AS (
    SELECT member_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(LOWER(TRIM(item)), '')) AS kind_count
    FROM item_parts
    GROUP BY member_id
),
spending AS (
    SELECT member_id, ROUND(SUM(cost), 2) AS total_spending_dollars
    FROM period_expenses
    GROUP BY member_id
),
ranked_members AS (
    SELECT m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name,
           i.kind_count,
           s.total_spending_dollars,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY i.kind_count DESC) AS kind_rank
    FROM main.member AS m
    JOIN item_counts AS i ON i.member_id = m.member_id
    JOIN spending AS s ON s.member_id = m.member_id
)
SELECT full_name, kind_count, total_spending_dollars
FROM ranked_members
WHERE kind_rank = 1
ORDER BY full_name
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH RECURSIVE period_expenses AS (
    SELECT e.link_to_member AS member_id,
           e.expense_description,
           e.cost
    FROM expense AS e
    WHERE e.expense_date >= '2019-10-01'
      AND e.expense_date < '2019-12-01'
),
split_items(member_id, item, remainder) AS (
    SELECT p.member_id, NULL, p.expense_description || ','
    FROM period_expenses AS p
    UNION ALL
    SELECT s.member_id,
           LOWER(TRIM(SUBSTR(s.remainder, 1, INSTR(s.remainder, ',') - 1))),
           SUBSTR(s.remainder, INSTR(s.remainder, ',') + 1)
    FROM split_items AS s
    WHERE s.remainder <> ''
),
item_counts AS (
    SELECT s.member_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.item) AS kind_count
    FROM split_items AS s
    WHERE s.item <> ''
    GROUP BY s.member_id
),
spending AS (
    SELECT p.member_id, ROUND(SUM(p.cost), 2) AS total_spending
    FROM period_expenses AS p
    GROUP BY p.member_id
),
ranked_members AS (
    SELECT m.member_id,
           m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name,
           i.kind_count,
           s.total_spending,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY i.kind_count DESC) AS kind_rank
    FROM member AS m
    JOIN item_counts AS i ON i.member_id = m.member_id
    JOIN spending AS s ON s.member_id = m.member_id
)
SELECT r.full_name, r.kind_count, r.total_spending
FROM ranked_members AS r
WHERE r.kind_rank = 1
ORDER BY r.full_name, r.member_id
LIMIT 1000

Final SQL / answer

WITH hero_power_counts AS (
    SELECT s.id, g.gender, COUNT(hp.power_id) AS power_count
    FROM main.superhero AS s
    JOIN main.gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id
    LEFT JOIN main.hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id
    WHERE g.gender = 'Male'
       OR (
           g.gender = 'Female'
           AND TRIM(s.full_name) LIKE '% %'
           AND TRIM(s.full_name) NOT IN (
               'Anna Marie',
               'Cyberdyne Systems Series X Terminator',
               'Diana of Themyscira'
           )
       )
    GROUP BY s.id, g.gender
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Male' THEN power_count END), 2) AS male_average,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'Female' THEN power_count END), 2) AS female_average
FROM hero_power_counts
LIMIT 1000

      "sql": "WITH power_counts AS (\n    SELECT hp.hero_id, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS power_count\n    FROM main.hero_power AS hp\n    LEFT JOIN main.superpower AS p ON p.id = hp.power_id\n    GROUP BY hp.hero_id\n),\nnames AS (\n    SELECT s.id, g.gender, s.superhero_name, TRIM(s.full_name) AS full_name, pc.record_count, pc.power_count\n    FROM main.superhero AS s\n    JOIN main.gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id\n    LEFT JOIN power_counts AS pc ON pc.hero_id = s.id\n    WHERE g.gender IN ('Male', 'Female')\n)\nSELECT gender, 'all heroes' AS category, COUNT(*) AS heroes,\n       COUNT(record_count) AS heroes_with_power_records, SUM(COALESCE(power_count, 0)) AS powers,\n       SUM(COALESCE(record_count - power_count, 0)) AS extra_power_records\nFROM names\nGROUP BY gender\nUNION ALL\nSELECT gender, 'space in full name', COUNT(*), COUNT(record_count), SUM(COALESCE(power_count, 0)),\n       SUM(COALESCE(record_count - power_count, 0))\nFROM names\nWHERE full_name LIKE '% %'\nGROUP BY gender\nUNION ALL\nSELECT gender, COALESCE(full_name, '[NULL]'), 1, record_count IS NOT NULL, COALESCE(power_count, 0),\n       COALESCE(record_count - power_count, 0)\nFROM names\nWHERE id IN (83, 341, 410, 431, 474, 557, 586, 587, 610, 632, 673, 674, 675, 676, 730, 735, 745)\n   OR (full_name NOT LIKE '% %' AND full_name GLOB '*[^a-zA-Z-]*')"
    },

Final SQL / answer

WITH hero_power_counts AS (
    SELECT s.id, g.gender, COUNT(hp.power_id) AS power_count
    FROM main.superhero AS s
    JOIN main.gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id
    LEFT JOIN main.hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id
    WHERE g.gender IN ('Male', 'Female')
      AND INSTR(TRIM(s.full_name), ' ') > 0
      AND TRIM(s.full_name) NOT IN (
          'Anna Marie',
          'Diana of Themyscira',
          'Howard (Last name unrevealed)',
          'Krypto the Superdog',
          'Mr. Mxyzptlk',
          'Ra''s Al Ghul',
          'Weapon XI',
          'Yurrd the Unknown'
      )
      AND TRIM(s.full_name) NOT LIKE 'Cyberdyne Systems Series %'
    GROUP BY s.id, g.gender
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(power_count) FILTER (WHERE gender = 'Male'), 2) AS male_average,
       ROUND(AVG(power_count) FILTER (WHERE gender = 'Female'), 2) AS female_average
FROM hero_power_counts
LIMIT 1

      "sql": "WITH name_groups AS (\n    SELECT g.gender, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT TRIM(s.full_name)) AS labels\n    FROM main.superhero AS s\n    JOIN main.gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id\n    WHERE g.gender IN ('Male', 'Female')\n      AND INSTR(TRIM(s.full_name), ' ') = 0\n    GROUP BY g.gender\n),\npower_quality AS (\n    SELECT COUNT(*) AS links,\n           COUNT(hp.power_id) AS nonnull_links,\n           COUNT(p.id) AS matched_links\n    FROM main.hero_power AS hp\n    LEFT JOIN main.superpower AS p ON p.id = hp.power_id\n),\nduplicate_links AS (\n    SELECT COUNT(*) AS duplicates\n    FROM (\n        SELECT hp.hero_id, hp.power_id\n        FROM main.hero_power AS hp\n        GROUP BY hp.hero_id, hp.power_id\n        HAVING COUNT(*) > 1\n    )\n)\nSELECT ng.gender, ng.labels, pq.links, pq.nonnull_links, pq.matched_links, dl.duplicates\nFROM name_groups AS ng\nCROSS JOIN power_quality AS pq\nCROSS JOIN duplicate_links AS dl"

  "question": "I'm preparing a report on Marvel's roster and want to gauge how heroic their catalogued heroes are. Final SQL / answer

SELECT ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*),
    2
) AS percentage_good
FROM main.superhero AS s
JOIN main.publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id
LEFT JOIN main.alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id
WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
  AND TRIM(s.full_name) NOT IN ('', '-', 'Howard (Last name unrevealed)', 'Weapon XI')
LIMIT 1

      "definition_check_id": "-pwE__z7I5JcSRSSSmyfXBd6kUmdLWI_aXFuiR4W7r0",
      "sql": "SELECT p.publisher_name, a.alignment, COUNT(*) AS total,\n       COUNT(s.full_name) AS nonnull_names,\n       COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(s.full_name), '')) AS nonblank_names,\n       COUNT(CASE WHEN TRIM(s.full_name) = '-' THEN 1 END) AS dashes,\n       COUNT(CASE WHEN TRIM(s.full_name) = s.superhero_name THEN 1 END) AS same_as_hero_name\nFROM main.superhero AS s\nJOIN main.publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id\nLEFT JOIN main.alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id\nWHERE p.publisher_name LIKE '%Marvel%'\nGROUP BY p.publisher_name, a.alignment\nORDER BY p.publisher_name, a.alignment"
    },
    "result": {
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "4 row(s):\nObserved value types (displayed rows): publisher_name=str; alignment=NoneType,str; total=int; nonnull_names=int; nonblank_names=int; dashes=int; same_as_hero_name=int\npublisher_name | alignment | total | nonnull_names | nonblank_names | dashes | same_as_hero_name\n--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---\nMarvel Comics | None | 3 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 0\nMarvel Comics | Bad | 118 | 105 | 105 | 26 | 10\nMarvel Comics | Good | 256 | 208 | 208 | 23 | 16\nMarvel Comics | Neutral | 10 | 8 | 8 | 3 | 0\nSQL: SELECT p.publisher_name, a.alignment, COUNT(*) AS total,\n       COUNT(s.full_name) AS nonnull_names,\n       COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(s.full_name), '')) AS nonblank_names,\n       COUNT(CASE WHEN TRIM(s.full_name) = '-' THEN 1 END) AS dashes,\n       COUNT(CASE WHEN TRIM(s.full_name) = s.superhero_name THEN 1 END) AS same_as_hero_name\nFROM main.superhero AS s\nJOIN main.publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id\nLEFT JOIN main.alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id\nWHERE p.publisher_name LIKE '%Marvel%'\nGROUP BY p.publisher_name, a.alignment\nORDER BY p.publisher_name, a.alignment\nLIMIT 1000"

{

  "db": "superhero",
  "question": "Among superheroes whose weight is not recorded, how many more have the 'No Colour' eye category than have blue eyes? I want a single whole number: the count of 'No Colour' eyes minus the count of blue eyes in that group - it can be negative if blue is more common. Please give me just that one number, with no other results or breakdowns.",
  "evidence": "'No Colour' is an eye category meaning the hero's eye colour is unspecified."
}

Final SQL / answer

SELECT
    COUNT(CASE WHEN c.colour = 'No Colour' THEN 1 END)
    - COUNT(CASE WHEN c.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 END) AS count_difference
FROM main.superhero AS s
JOIN main.colour AS c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id
WHERE s.weight_kg IS NULL
LIMIT 1

SELECT ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN p.SEX = 'F' THEN 1 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
    2
) AS female_percentage
FROM main.Patient AS p
WHERE DATE(p.Birthday) <= DATE('2026-10-09', '-56 years')
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM main.Laboratory AS l
      WHERE l.ID = p.ID
        AND l.PT >= 14
  )
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH RECURSIVE diagnosis_entries (ID, remaining, disease) AS (
    SELECT p.ID,
           CASE
               WHEN trim(p.Diagnosis) = 'SJS  RA' THEN 'SJS,RA'
               ELSE replace(p.Diagnosis, char(29), ',')
           END || ',',
           NULL
    FROM main.Patient AS p
    WHERE instr(p.Diagnosis, 'RA') > 0
      AND instr(p.Diagnosis, 'SJS') > 0

    UNION ALL

    SELECT e.ID,
           substr(e.remaining, instr(e.remaining, ',') + 1),
           trim(substr(e.remaining, 1, instr(e.remaining, ',') - 1),
                char(9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 32))
    FROM diagnosis_entries AS e
    WHERE e.remaining <> ''
),
overlap_patients AS (
    SELECT e.ID
    FROM diagnosis_entries AS e
    WHERE e.disease <> ''
      AND e.disease NOT GLOB '* susp'
      AND e.disease NOT GLOB '* susp.'
    GROUP BY e.ID
    HAVING MAX(e.disease = 'RA') = 1
       AND MAX(e.disease = 'SJS') = 1
       AND MAX(e.disease NOT IN ('RA', 'SJS')) = 0
),
patients_with_normal_platelets AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.ID
    FROM main.Laboratory AS l
    WHERE l.PLT > 100
      AND l.PLT < 400
)
SELECT COUNT(n.ID) AS patients_ever_normal,
       COUNT(*) - COUNT(n.ID) AS patients_never_normal
FROM overlap_patients AS p
LEFT JOIN patients_with_normal_platelets AS n ON n.ID = p.ID
LIMIT 1

WITH RECURSIVE diagnosis_tokens(patient_id, diagnosis, remaining) AS (
    SELECT Patient.ID,
           '',
           CASE trim(Patient.Diagnosis, char(9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 32))
               WHEN 'SJS  RA' THEN 'SJS,RA'
               WHEN 'RA  SJS' THEN 'RA,SJS'
               ELSE replace(Patient.Diagnosis, char(29), ',')
           END || ','
    FROM Patient
    WHERE instr(Patient.Diagnosis, 'RA') > 0
      AND instr(Patient.Diagnosis, 'SJS') > 0

    UNION ALL

    SELECT patient_id,
           trim(substr(remaining, 1, instr(remaining, ',') - 1),
                char(9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 32)),
           substr(remaining, instr(remaining, ',') + 1)
    FROM diagnosis_tokens
    WHERE remaining <> ''
),
eligible_patients AS (
    SELECT patient_id
    FROM diagnosis_tokens
    WHERE diagnosis <> ''
      AND rtrim(diagnosis, '.') NOT LIKE '% susp'
    GROUP BY patient_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT diagnosis) = 2
       AND MIN(diagnosis) = 'RA'
       AND MAX(diagnosis) = 'SJS'
),
normal_platelet_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT Laboratory.ID
    FROM Laboratory
    WHERE Laboratory.PLT > 100
      AND Laboratory.PLT < 400
)
SELECT COUNT(normal_platelet_patients.ID) AS patients_with_normal_platelets,
       COUNT(*) - COUNT(normal_platelet_patients.ID) AS patients_without_normal_platelets
FROM eligible_patients
LEFT JOIN normal_platelet_patients
    ON normal_platelet_patients.ID = eligible_patients.patient_id
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

SELECT e."Symptoms", p."Diagnosis"
FROM "Examination" AS e
JOIN "Patient" AS p ON p."ID" = e."ID"
WHERE TRIM(e."Symptoms", CHAR(9, 10, 13, 32)) <> ''
  AND p."Birthday" IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (
    WITH RECURSIVE disease_list(remaining) AS (
      SELECT REPLACE(e."Diagnosis", '+', ',') || ','
      UNION ALL
      SELECT SUBSTR(remaining, INSTR(remaining, ',') + 1)
      FROM disease_list
      WHERE remaining <> ''
    )
    SELECT 1
    FROM disease_list
    WHERE TRIM(
      SUBSTR(remaining, 1, INSTR(remaining, ',') - 1),
      CHAR(9, 10, 13, 32)
    ) = 'SLE'
  )
ORDER BY p."Birthday" DESC, p."ID" ASC, e."Examination Date" DESC
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

SELECT e."Symptoms", p."Diagnosis" AS "Overall Diagnosis"
FROM main."Examination" AS e
JOIN main."Patient" AS p ON p."ID" = e."ID"
WHERE INSTR(',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(e."Diagnosis", ' ', ''), '+', ',') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0
  AND NULLIF(TRIM(e."Symptoms"), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND p."Birthday" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY p."Birthday" DESC, p."ID" ASC, e."Examination Date" DESC
LIMIT 1

Final SQL / answer

WITH sexes(sex_code, sex) AS (
    VALUES ('M', 'Male'), ('F', 'Female')
),
patients_with_high_alt AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.ID
    FROM main.Laboratory AS l
    WHERE l.GPT >= 60
)
SELECT s.sex,
       COUNT(p.ID) FILTER (WHERE h.ID IS NULL) AS patient_count
FROM sexes AS s
LEFT JOIN main.Patient AS p ON p.SEX = s.sex_code
LEFT JOIN patients_with_high_alt AS h ON h.ID = p.ID
GROUP BY s.sex_code, s.sex
ORDER BY s.sex_code DESC
LIMIT 1000

      FROM main.Laboratory AS l
      WHERE l.ID = p.ID

ORDER BY p.SEX DESC

WITH requested_types(bond_type, sort_order) AS (
    VALUES ('-', 1), ('=', 2), ('#', 3)
),
bond_counts AS (
    SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT b.bond_id) AS bond_count
    FROM main.bond AS b
    JOIN main.molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id
    JOIN main.connected AS c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id
    JOIN main.atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id
    JOIN main.atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2
    WHERE m.label = '+'
      AND a1.element = 'c'
      AND a2.element = 'c'
      AND b.bond_type IN ('-', '=', '#')
    GROUP BY b.bond_type
)
SELECT t.bond_type, COALESCE(bc.bond_count, 0) AS bond_count
FROM requested_types AS t
LEFT JOIN bond_counts AS bc ON bc.bond_type = t.bond_type
ORDER BY t.sort_order
LIMIT 1000

WITH bond_types(bond_type, sort_order) AS (
    VALUES ('-', 1), ('=', 2), ('#', 3)
),
carbon_carbon_bonds AS (
    SELECT b.bond_id, b.bond_type
    FROM main.bond AS b
    JOIN main.molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id
    JOIN main.connected AS c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id
    JOIN main.atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id
    JOIN main.atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2
    WHERE m.label = '+'
      AND a1.element = 'c'
      AND a2.element = 'c'
)
SELECT t.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT b.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM bond_types AS t
LEFT JOIN carbon_carbon_bonds AS b ON b.bond_type = t.bond_type
GROUP BY t.bond_type, t.sort_order
ORDER BY t.sort_order
LIMIT 1000
